body:
> Note: this issue text was drafted with the help of the Claude AI agent.

### Summary

We run a self-hosted GitLab. Each project there gets its own package registry, and we have eleven internal
Python packages in eleven projects, so we have eleven separate indexes. Every machine that uses those
packages gets the same `uv.toml`, listing all eleven.

Three of our package names are also taken by unrelated projects on PyPI. For those three, `uvx <name>`
installs our package only if we happened to list its index first. Otherwise uv installs the PyPI package
instead, and the same thing happens to any internal dependency of the tool being installed.

Whichever index is first also answers for the other two packages, because it forwards anything it does not
host to PyPI. So those two come from PyPI.

uv reports no error. If the PyPI package provides a command with the same name, `uvx <name>` runs that
command instead of ours.

### Why it happens

An index and a source do different jobs. An index tells uv that a registry exists and should be searched. A
source tells uv that a particular package name comes from a particular registry. Only a source affects which
registry a package is taken from, and a source can only be written in two places:

| | `pyproject.toml` | PEP 723 | `uv.toml` | CLI |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| index | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| source | yes | yes | no | no |

`uvx` and `uv tool install` have no project and no script metadata, so neither of those two places is
available to them. We can list our registries, and we cannot say which package comes from which registry. uv
then searches the indexes in order and takes the first answer.

That first answer can come from a registry that does not hold the package at all. When a GitLab registry is
asked for a name it does not have, it forwards the request to PyPI and returns what PyPI sends back. This is
on by default, and we cannot disable it because we are on the GitLab Free tier.

So the first registry in our list answers for any name PyPI knows. Our eight uniquely named packages are
fine, because PyPI returns nothing for them and the search moves on to the registry that holds them. The
three names PyPI also has are the ones we lose.

We could collapse this to one index by moving the projects into a GitLab group, which serves an index across
all of its projects. That would avoid the problem, and it should not be necessary. Several indexes is a
normal configuration and uv should resolve correctly with more than one.

### `explicit = true` does not help

An index marked `explicit = true` is only used for packages that a source assigns to it. Outside a project
there are no sources, so an explicit index is never used. Marking our registries explicit would leave `uvx`
unable to find our packages at all.

### What would fix it

We are going to rename the three that clash. Yet we do need a way to guarantee that a package always comes
from our own indexes, using uv alone. A package with the same name may be published at any time on PyPI.

1. Accept sources in `uv.toml`. `uv.lock` already records the registry each package resolved from, as
   `source = { registry = "..." }`, so a source written outside `pyproject.toml` would be captured in the
   lock like any other resolution. We want our internal packages and their indexes in the lockfile.
2. Accept a source on the command line, for example
   `uvx --index reg=<url> --source internal-dep=reg --from internal-tool internal-tool`.
3. Have `uv tool install <path>` read the target project's `[tool.uv]`.

### Related issues

- #6772 — sources in `uv.toml`
- #12013 — configuring dependency sources locally
- #18053 — a `pyproject.toml` source cannot name an index declared in `uv.toml`
- #16021 — installing a tool that contains packages from a private index
- #11522 — `uv tool install` has no index configuration of its own
- #8758 — pinning a package to an index with no fallback

### Workaround

A PEP 723 script replaces `uvx` for us as it supports inline script metadata to define sources:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --no-project --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.15"
# dependencies = ["internal-tool", "internal-dep"]
#
# [[tool.uv.index]]
# name = "reg-a"
# url = "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/1/packages/pypi/simple"
# explicit = true
#
# [[tool.uv.index]]
# name = "reg-b"
# url = "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/2/packages/pypi/simple"
# explicit = true
#
# [tool.uv.sources]
# internal-tool = { index = "reg-a" }
# internal-dep = { index = "reg-b" }
# ///
import internal_dep
import internal_tool

internal_tool.main(internal_dep)
```

### Version

uv 0.12.5, Linux, GitLab 19.3.0 Free with request forwarding enabled.
title: uvx should be able to load packages from different internal indexes
